doc_verification.detail: Reachability: no doc_preflight.json sidecar exists anywhere near the contract; contract endpoint_registry records source_status=reachable with verified_at 2026-09-02T12:34:08Z, and the live page was successfully fetched via the alternate web reader (WebFetch itself returned domain_blocked for api.qdrant.tech, recorded honestly; content was still obtained, so not treated as FAIL). Version: live page version selector shows v1.18.x and canonical URL is /v-1-18-x/..., matching target 1.18.0 on major.minor. Content: the live page documents POST /cluster/recover with exactly ONE response, '200 Successful' (usage/time/status/result envelope), matching the behavioral assertion's 'HTTP 200'; HOWEVER the registry's recorded doc_quote ('Removes cluster metadata and restarts as a single-node cluster from local data; irrecoverable for removed peers; use only when quorum is permanently lost.') does NOT appear on the live page — current prose is 'Attempts to restore or synchronize the node's current state with that of its peers.' (Fern docs rebuild drift); and the page documents NOTHING about standalone mode, distributed-mode prerequisites, or any non-200 disposition (the in-repo openapi/openapi-cluster.ytt.yaml:38-44 likewise documents only a boolean 200 response, summary 'Tries to recover current peer Raft state.'). Endpoint precision: endpoint_registry entry cluster+recover POST (admin) present at structured_contract.json line 4048 plus doc_quote registry entry at line 5682; live path and script URL (from raw_knowledge api_endpoints[].url) all agree.

http_semantics.note: The mode-inapplicable recover call was refused as HTTP 500 'Service internal error: Qdrant is running in standalone mode' — not 2xx-masked. Status-class inconsistency within the same family: the same deployment-mode refusal on /cluster/peer/{peer_id} is a 400 'Bad request: Distributed mode disabled.' while recover uses the 5xx ServiceError class. All writer-plane data calls in this log were clean 2xx.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: HTTP 200 on cluster recovery (dangerous operational op)
contract_grounding.note: Violates-declaration self-check: the claim's phenomenon is a REFUSAL (500), not a silent acceptance, and the quoted assertion claims 'HTTP 200' — the API returned 500 on this deployment, so violates=true records a genuine deviation from the only documented disposition. Constraint linkage: the candidates.jsonl dispatch field constraint_id was EMPTY (mechanical extraction gap); the script header (debate_logs/state_cluster_recover_003.py line 6) declares 'constraint_ids: qdrant_state_cluster_recover_001, qdrant_behavioral_cluster_recover_001', both present in structured_contract.json (lines 6759 and 7647). The behavioral entry is the primary anchor for the observed 500-disposition (its contract description reads verbatim: 'returns 200 ok; intended for use only when quorum is permanently lost'). The co-anchored state constraint qdrant_state_cluster_recover_001 (assertion verbatim: 'cluster recovery resets the peer to a single-node cluster from local data; it is destructive for cluster membership state') was NOT violated — recovery never executed; final count 45==45 and describe green prove accepted-write durability and intact state. The deviation is deployment-mode-conditional (standalone) and source-shown designed — see source_grounding; by-design weighing belongs to the auditor.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: POST /cluster/recover -> cluster_api.rs:60-73 recover_current_peer -> toc/mod.rs:546-551 request_snapshot() -> toc/mod.rs:775-779 get_consensus_proposal_sender() -> consensus_proposal_sender is None because src/main.rs:508-514 constructs it as None when settings.cluster.enabled=false (the harness container testvdb-qdrant-standalone per deployment_meta.json) -> StorageError::service_error("Qdrant is running in standalone mode") -> errors.rs:21 Display 'Service internal error: {description}' -> actix maps ServiceError to HTTP 500 with envelope {"status":{"error":...}} — exactly the observed body. The recover operation is consensus-based by nature (it proposes a Raft snapshot operation through the consensus channel); in standalone mode no consensus exists, so the call cannot apply.

excluded: concurrency race — writer plane fully clean: 40/40 wait=true upserts accepted, 0 rejected_4xx, 0 err_5xx, 0 transport, 0 thread errors (tally line 9); final count 45 == expected 45

mundane_explanation.surviving: deployment-mode dependence: the harness deployed qdrant standalone (container testvdb-qdrant-standalone, settings.cluster.enabled=false, GET /cluster reports status 'disabled'), and the 500 is the source-designed gate for consensus-only operations on a node without consensus (explicit comment main.rs:512 'We don't need sender for the single-node mode'). Whether an UNDOCUMENTED 500 on a distributed-only endpoint — while the same-family /cluster/peer/{peer_id} answers the identical standalone condition with a documented-class 400 'Distributed mode disabled.' — is a genuine product defect (wrong status class / doc gap) or an environment mismatch (testing a distributed-mode endpoint on a standalone deployment) is the auditor's call; both facts are source- and log-anchored above.
